stories.title: Tennessee Hosts Fall Ball Weekend — Pickens and Mardjetko Lead Home Stand
stories.angle: After a road trip to MTSU (Oct 18, 3 PM ET), Tennessee returns home to Sherri Parker Lee Stadium for a full fall ball weekend with three programs. Karlyn Pickens (AUSL No. 1 pick, 194 K, 1.70 ERA in 2026) and Sage Mardjetko (16-3, 1.26 ERA, NFCA All-American) anchor what Karen Weekly calls the deepest staff in program history. Emma Clarke's cycle performance earlier this fall signals a potent offense to match.

#GBO #TNSoftball

facebook.long_form:
After a road trip to MTSU on Sunday, Tennessee softball is back home at Sherri Parker Lee Stadium in Knoxville.

The Lady Vols are hosting their third fall weekend of the 2026 season this week, with Northeast Alabama, Northwest Florida State, and Roane State all making the trip east. For fans anywhere near Knoxville, it's a no-brainer — free admission to watch a legitimate national title contender play October softball.

Head coach Karen Weekly hasn't been shy about her enthusiasm for this group. She has called this the deepest pitching staff in program history. When you see who's out there, you understand why.

Karlyn Pickens is back. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 AUSL College Draft — who posted 194 strikeouts and a 1.70 ERA in her final spring season — didn't have to come back. She chose to. Running alongside her is Sage Mardjetko, who went 16-3 with a 1.26 ERA and earned NFCA All-American honors last spring. Most programs would build their entire development plan around one of them. Tennessee has both.

And that's before you get to the offense. Sophomore Emma Clarke already announced her presence this fall with a rare cycle — home run, triple, two doubles, and six RBI in a 32-0 exhibition win over Tusculum. That kind of October performance tells you something about what's coming in February.

Tennessee is building for another WCWS run. This week's home fall games are your chance to see it in person — for free.
facebook.image_caption: Tennessee fall ball is back home at Sherri Parker Lee Stadium. Northeast Alabama, NW Florida State, and Roane State in Knoxville this week. Pickens + Mardjetko + Clarke — free admission. Don't miss it.

article.headline: Tennessee Brings the Fall Ball Home: Pickens, Mardjetko Lead Lady Vols Home Stand

stories.title: Oklahoma State Lands Top-100 2028 Infielder Peyton Cleary
stories.angle: Oklahoma State and head coach Kenny Gajewski secured a commitment from Peyton Cleary, a top-100 2028 infielder from Liberty North High School (Missouri). Cleary is OSU's first 2028 commitment and arrives as one of the Cowgirls' highest-rated prospects in recent years. The announcement coincides with the end of the two-day contact window (Oct 17-18).

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Oklahoma State softball has its first 2028 commit.

Infielder Peyton Cleary (top-100, Liberty North MO) is headed to Stillwater to play for Kenny Gajewski.

Contact window just closed — OSU didn't wait long.

#OKState #Cowgirls

facebook.long_form:
Oklahoma State softball made its first move in the Class of 2028 on Sunday night.

Head coach Kenny Gajewski and the Cowgirls secured a commitment from Peyton Cleary, a top-100 infielder from Liberty North High School in Missouri — and the timing was no accident. The announcement came as the NCAA's two-day contact window for the 2028 class (Oct. 17-18) was closing. OSU used the access, and Cleary is the result.

She's the Cowgirls' first 2028 pledge, and she arrives with a profile that earned national attention. Liberty North is a school with strong softball history, and Cleary fits the mold of the high-IQ infielder that Gajewski has consistently prioritized in building OSU's roster.

The 2028 class nationally is already loaded at the top. Texas leads with No. 1-ranked infielder Michaela Landers, Ainsley Morvan (22 HR as a high schooler), and two others — all from the TX Bombers Gold program. Oklahoma has five commitments. Florida has No. 2-ranked Kylie Holden and catcher Evans. Florida State just landed twins Keira and Kelsey Luderer over the same contact window weekend.

OSU's move with Cleary is exactly the kind of decisive recruiting that separates programs in the modern landscape. The Class of 2028 won't step on campus for two more years, but the decisions being made right now will define where programs stand in the late 2020s.
facebook.image_caption: Oklahoma State has its first commitment in the Class of 2028. Top-100 infielder Peyton Cleary (Liberty North, MO) is headed to Stillwater to play for Kenny Gajewski and the Cowgirls.

article.headline: Oklahoma State Lands Top-100 Infielder Peyton Cleary in Class of 2028

stories.title: OU Battle Series Game 4 — Two Days Away, Wednesday at Love's Field
stories.angle: OU's fall showcase continues Wednesday at Love's Field (6:30 PM CT, 1oklahoma.com). The Sooners feature one of the nation's deepest rosters: Jordy Kavan (2x WCWS MOP), Grace Wells (39 HR, NFCA Freshman of Year 2026), Sydney Berzon, Cruz, and Ludlow. Game 5 vs. USAO follows Oct 23.

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Two days. Love's Field. Wednesday, 6:30 PM CT.

Kavan (2x WCWS MOP) and Wells (39 HR, NFCA Freshman of Year) in the same fall lineup.

Stream: 1oklahoma.com

#Sooners #OUSoftball

facebook.long_form:
Wednesday night at Love's Field.

OU's Battle Series Game 4 is set for October 21, 6:30 p.m. Central, and the roster Patty Gasso is bringing to the field might be the most decorated in the program's fall history.

Grace Wells — the 2026 NFCA Freshman of the Year who hit 39 home runs in her debut season — is back in the box. Jordy Kavan, a two-time Women's College World Series Most Outstanding Player, is back in the lineup. Sydney Berzon anchors the pitching staff that has been dominant all fall. Add Cruz and Ludlow, and the Sooners go deep across every position on the field.

The fall opener at Love's Field drew 2,351 fans — remarkable for an October exhibition — and left Gasso visibly emotional. The response from the fanbase has matched what the program has put on the field: this team has earned the excitement.

Stream Game 4 on 1oklahoma.com. Game 5 of the series follows Thursday, October 23 against USAO.

If you haven't seen this roster in action yet, Wednesday night is your opportunity. It's the kind of lineup that you'll want to say you watched in October when they're playing in Knoxville next June.
facebook.image_caption: OU Battle Series Game 4: Wednesday, Oct. 21 at Love's Field, 6:30 PM CT. Kavan + Wells in the same lineup — stream on 1oklahoma.com. Don't miss it.

article.headline: OU Battle Series Game 4: Kavan, Wells, and the Best Roster in Fall Softball Play Wednesday

stories.title: 2028 Recruiting — Contact Window Closes, Commit Wave Begins
stories.angle: The first contact period for the Class of 2028 closed yesterday (Oct 18), but its effects are just beginning. Programs had 48 hours to meet with junior prospects face-to-face. Texas enters this week as the class leader (Michaela Landers No. 1 IF, Ainsley Morvan 22 HR, Abdullah, Schellhammer all from TX Bombers Gold). OU has 5 commits, Florida has Holden (No. 2) + Evans (C), Oklahoma State just landed Peyton Cleary (top-100 infielder). A wave of announcements is expected Oct 19-21.

x_posts.label: Post 4-1
x_posts.text:
The 2028 contact window closed. The commit wave starts now.

Texas leads: No. 1 Michaela Landers + Ainsley Morvan (22 HR). OU has 5 commits. Florida has Holden (No. 2) + Evans. OSU just landed Peyton Cleary.

#d1softball #Recruiting

x_posts.label: Post 4-2
x_posts.text:
2028 class is forming fast.

Oklahoma State: Peyton Cleary (top-100 IF, Missouri)
Florida State: twins Keira and Kelsey Luderer
Texas: leading nationally with Landers + Morvan

Contact window is closed. Commit wave this week.

#d1softball

facebook.long_form:
The first contact window for the Class of 2028 closed Saturday. For 48 hours, D1 coaches had their first chance to meet face-to-face with high school juniors. Now the wave builds.

Commit announcements are expected through mid-week as recruits process what they experienced and finalize decisions. Here's where the class stands heading into Monday:

Texas is winning. The Longhorns hold the class's top position with No. 1-ranked infielder Michaela Landers already committed, along with Ainsley Morvan (22 home runs), Abdullah, and Schellhammer — all from TX Bombers Gold. If Texas adds to this group, they're tracking toward a legitimate No. 1 national class.

Oklahoma has five commitments and the resources to add more. Florida secured No. 2-ranked Kylie Holden (five-star, Michigan) and catcher Evans. Florida State added twins Keira and Kelsey Luderer in the contact weekend. Oklahoma State just landed top-100 infielder Peyton Cleary from Liberty North, Missouri.

The early signing period for softball opens November 11 — giving programs about three weeks to finalize their 2028 commitments before recruits can officially sign. The next few days will produce the clearest picture of where each program stands after the contact window sprint.

It's a great time to follow recruiting if you haven't been. The Class of 2028 is going to be special.
facebook.image_caption: The 2028 contact window is closed. The commit wave is starting. Texas leads nationally — but OU, Florida, OSU, and FSU are all building serious classes. Watch this space this week.

article.headline: 2028 Softball Recruiting: What Happened After the Contact Window Closed

stories.title: Transfer Portal Week 3 — Kasidi Pickering Still Undecided
stories.angle: With fall exhibitions well underway, most programs have filled their roster gaps through the transfer portal. But high-profile infielder Kasidi Pickering (Texas Tech, one of the top portal bats available) remains uncommitted, with OU and TTU still the primary destinations per reports. LSU's portal class (Winchell + Pickens twins) and OU's additions (Harter, Hansen, Gregus) are among the fall's most active hauls.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Still the biggest name in the portal: Kasidi Pickering hasn't committed yet.

OU and Texas Tech are the reported options. 137+ portal entries total.

A decision could come any day.

#d1softball #TransferPortal

facebook.long_form:
The fall transfer portal is winding down — but one major name is still out there.

Kasidi Pickering, the Texas Tech infielder and one of the fall portal's most coveted bats, remains uncommitted. Oklahoma and Texas Tech are the reported options, with no announcement made as of Monday.

Her decision matters. Pickering is the kind of infielder whose defensive range and offensive production would immediately strengthen whichever program lands her in the Big 12. For Oklahoma — already loaded with Wells, Kavan, and a deep returning core — adding Pickering would create a positional depth few rosters can match. For Texas Tech under new coaches Cottrill and Pendley — rebuilding from last season's transition — landing Pickering would signal that the new staff's momentum is real.

The broader portal picture shows how much the landscape has shifted. LSU assembled one of the cycle's top hauls: Mickey Winchell (.335 BA, 14 stolen bases from Notre Dame), plus twins Madison Pickens (Louisville) and Mackenzie Pickens (Ole Miss). OU added Harter, Hansen, and Gregus. The 137-plus total entries reflect how active the fall portal has been league-wide.

Most of the major decisions have been made. Pickering is the last significant story. A commitment is expected before the end of October.
facebook.image_caption: Kasidi Pickering — Texas Tech infielder, one of the top portal bats available — is still uncommitted. OU and Texas Tech are the reported options. Her decision could come any day.

article.headline: Fall Transfer Portal Watch: Kasidi Pickering Remains the Biggest Name Available
